skill.name: exploratory-data-analysis
skill.description: Analyze scientific data files, detect file formats, extract metadata, assess data quality, and generate markdown exploratory data analysis reports.
skill.summary: Analyze scientific datasets and generate format-aware EDA reports.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by scientific terminology, markdown code formatting, and legitimate local file analysis behavior. The analyzer reads user-provided local scientific data, extracts metadata and summaries, and writes a markdown report; no shell execution, network reconnaissance, credential access, prompt injection, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Reports include the absolute local input path.
remediation.suggestion: Consider making full path output optional or defaulting to the filename only to reduce accidental disclosure when reports are shared.

remediation.issue: The output report path can be supplied by the user.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the report writer may overwrite an existing file at the chosen path, or add an overwrite confirmation in interactive use.

content.value_statement: Scientific datasets often arrive in specialized formats that are hard to inspect quickly. This skill detects the format, summarizes contents, checks quality, and produces a clear EDA report.
actual_capabilities: Detects scientific file categories from extensions across chemistry, genomics, imaging, spectroscopy, omics, and general data files.
Reads reference guidance for more than 200 scientific file formats.
Analyzes common local formats such as CSV, TSV, JSON, NumPy arrays, HDF5, FASTA, FASTQ, TIFF, and standard images.
Computes basic metadata, dimensions, data types, missing values, and summary statistics where supported.
Generates a structured markdown report with file details, analysis results, findings, and recommended next steps.
Provides format-specific library suggestions and troubleshooting guidance for missing dependencies.
limitations: Some specialized formats require optional Python libraries that may not be installed.
Very large files may be sampled instead of fully loaded into memory.
Unknown or vendor-specific formats may require user-provided format details.
The generated report is descriptive and does not replace domain expert validation.

use_cases.title: Inspect a new sequencing dataset
use_cases.description: Identify FASTA or FASTQ structure, summarize sequence counts and lengths, and recommend quality-control steps.

use_cases.title: Review microscopy image metadata
use_cases.description: Summarize image dimensions, channels, value ranges, and downstream image-analysis recommendations.

use_cases.title: Profile a general experiment table
use_cases.description: Load CSV or TSV files, inspect columns, missing values, data types, and basic numerical summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze one data file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single local file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this scientific data file and create an exploratory data analysis summary: <path-to-file>.

prompt_templates.title: Assess data quality
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of completeness and quality issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run an EDA pass on <path-to-file>. Focus on missing values, invalid values, dimensions, metadata consistency, and quality concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Compare related files
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a small dataset collection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related files and summarize their differences, shared structure, and recommended integration steps: <file-list>.

prompt_templates.title: Plan downstream analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that connects EDA to next methods.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform format-aware EDA on <path-to-file>, then recommend preprocessing, visualization, statistical analysis, and validation steps for the dataset.

output_examples.input: Analyze reads.fastq for basic quality and structure.
output_examples.output: A markdown report describing FASTQ format, sampled read count, length range, mean quality, GC-related recommendations, and next quality-control steps.

output_examples.input: Explore experiment_results.csv and identify data quality issues.
output_examples.output: A tabular EDA summary with row and column counts, inferred data types, missing-value counts, numeric summaries, and suggested cleaning steps.
An imaging report with dimensions, mode, value range, page count when available, and recommendations for segmentation and intensity normalization.

best_practices: Provide the exact local file path and any known instrument or experiment context.
Install the relevant scientific Python libraries before analyzing specialized formats.
Review generated reports before sharing because they may include filenames and local path details.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as the only validation step for regulated or clinical datasets.
Do not load very large files fully when sampling or chunked processing is safer.
Do not assume unknown vendor formats are supported without checking the reference guidance.

faq.question: What types of files can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It covers chemistry, genomics, microscopy, spectroscopy, proteomics, metabolomics, and common scientific formats such as CSV, JSON, HDF5, TIFF, and NumPy arrays.

faq.question: Does it modify my data files?
faq.answer: No. The analyzer reads input data and writes a separate markdown report.

faq.question: Can it handle large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, but large files may need sampling, chunked processing, or memory-mapped access to avoid high memory use.

faq.question: What happens if a required library is missing?
faq.answer: The report includes a clear error message and suggests the library needed for that format.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed for Claude Code and also declares support for Claude and Codex workflows.

faq.question: Does the report include recommendations?
faq.answer: Yes. Reports include next steps for preprocessing, visualization, analysis methods, and format-specific quality checks.
